newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber ends down on weak housing report.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber ends down on weak housing report.

text.p: March CME lumber futures remained under pressure from the U.S. housing starts report and finished lower while back months posted small gains on spread action, traders said.
A smaller than expected rise in January housing starts over December's numnber weighed on March. A slow cash market also weighed on sentiment, traders said.

The Commerce Department reported January housing starts up 2.0 percent at 1.350 million units, below analyst expectations of 1.42 million. The figure may signal a slowdown in housing, they said after the report.
Rolling of long March positions into back months kept deferreds above previous levels. ING notably bought May and sold March, pit sources said.
Lumber closed $4.70 per tbf lower to $2.30 higher with only March off at $406.80 and May up $1.30 at $390.00.
